# Word RAM

 [Add links](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q48970419#sitelinks-wikipedia)                          From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [theoretical computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_computer_science), the **word RAM** (word random-access machine) model is a [model of computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_of_computation) in which a [random-access machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random-access_machine) does arithmetic and bitwise operations on a word of w bits. [Michael Fredman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fredman) and [Dan Willard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Willard) created it in 1990 to simulate programming languages like [C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language)).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-Fredman90-1)

## Model

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Word_RAM&action=edit&section=1)]

The word RAM model is an [abstract machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_machine) similar to a [random-access machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random-access_machine), but with finite memory and word-length. It works with words of size up to w bits, meaning it can store [integers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integer_(computing)) up to      2  w   − 1   {\displaystyle 2^{w}-1}  . Because the model assumes that the [word size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_size) matches the problem size, that is, for a problem of size n,     w ≥ log ⁡ n   {\displaystyle w\geq \log n}  , the word RAM model is a [transdichotomous model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transdichotomous_model).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-2) The model allows both arithmetic operations and [bitwise operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operations) including [logical shifts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_shift) to be done in [constant time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_time) (the precise instruction set assumed by an algorithm or proof using the model may vary).

## Algorithms and data structures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Word_RAM&action=edit&section=2)]

In the word RAM model, [integer sorting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integer_sorting) can be done fairly efficiently. Yijie Han and [Mikkel Thorup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikkel_Thorup) created a [randomized algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randomized_algorithm) to sort integers in [expected time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_time) of (in [Big O notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_O_notation))     O ( n   log ⁡ log ⁡ n   )   {\displaystyle O(n{\sqrt {\log \log n}})}  ,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-Han02-3) while Han also created a [deterministic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_algorithm) variant with [running time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_time)     O ( n log ⁡ log ⁡ n )   {\displaystyle O(n\log \log n)}  .[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-Han04-4)

The [dynamic predecessor problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_predecessor_problem) is also commonly analyzed in the word RAM model, and was the original motivation for the model. [Dan Willard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Willard) used [y-fast tries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y-fast_trie) to solve this in     O ( log ⁡ w )   {\displaystyle O(\log w)}   time, or, more precisely,     O ( log ⁡ log ⁡ U )   {\displaystyle O(\log \log U)}   where U is a bound on the values stored.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-5) [Michael Fredman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fredman) and Willard also solved the problem using [fusion trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusion_tree) in     O (  log  w   ⁡ n )   {\displaystyle O(\log _{w}n)}   time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-Fredman90-1) Using [exponential search trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_tree), a query can be performed in     O (   log ⁡ n  /  log ⁡ log ⁡ n   )   {\displaystyle O({\sqrt {\log n/\log \log n}})}  .[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_RAM#cite_note-6)

Additional results in the word RAM model are listed in the article on [range searching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_searching).

Lower bounds applicable to word RAM algorithms are often proved in the [cell-probe model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell-probe_model).
